title: XR stuttering / frame pacing issues
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.6 and 4.7, haven't had time to test more versions

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable (5b4e0cb0f) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1062) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 31.74 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Basically it seems like Godot is handling the Frame Pacing in OpenXR wrongly. There is an issue on this already #91945 but I am unsure if it is related or not.

What happens is occasionally we get stutters where it seems the FPS drops for a brief frame or two. In my case I can see delta going from 11.11ms (90hz) up to 20-30ms. From my testing there isn't exactly a thing that causes these stutters but it seems more prevalent in heavier scenes. And even without these stutters the FPS / Delta seems to be all over the place at 90hz so 11.11ms the Delta can go up to 16ms and down to 3ms from my testing.

Things I have tried and ruled out:

1. It's not my scripts as it happens in empty scenes / new projects.
2. It affects the entire game, not just process or physics process.
3. Profiler reads these stutterings as a phantom delta, meaning there is no actual cause / given reason for this delta where adding up all the deltas from each task that took place doesn't add up to actual delta when the spike happens.
4. Deltas I see are normal 11.1ms (for 90hz) but sudden spikes to 20-30ms.
5. It seems to happen more often in heavier scenes even though we have the frame budget.
6. I have tried using Separate Rendering thread and it has had some help but not a fix.
7. I have ruled out wireless connection issues, Virtual desktop and Steamlink.
8. I have tried ALVR wired and still see stuttering.
9. VSYNC on my display is disabled on _ready but have tried it enabled and I have tried setting my display refresh rate in windows settings to different ones(60, 120, 144, 240).
10. I have tried disabling multiwindow in editor.
11. These stutterings happen when moving headset and also at standstill.
12. Using XRFrameTools to judge what is happening. Only reading is CPU Wait that spikes during stuttering.
13. Using SteamLinks frame debugger, seeing similar CPU wait thing.
14. Nothing to do with Physics frame so turning interpolation on/off does nothing, same goes for jitter fix.
15. Turned off delta smoothing.
16. Turned off Max FPS, and also setting it to headset refresh rate.
17. Tried all three rendering modes, Forward+, Mobile and Compatibility.
18. Tried Vulkan and D3D12.
19. It is not window de-prioritization.
20. It is not E Core scheduling or process affinitiy or process priority.
21. It is not Windows Timer resolution, I have ruled this out by having a custom fork with it changed.
22. Not low processor mode.
23. Fullscreen doesn't help.
24. Minimizing window doesn't help.
25. Fullscreen optimization / GPU hardware schedule doesn't help.
26. No frame interpolation / frame warp / ASW / SSW is enabled.
27. Built for Quest 3 standalone and still seeing same issues.
28. The most interesting part is that setting Engine.max_fps to refresh rate doesn't seem to change the behaviour when compared to Engine.max_fps = 0. However setting it to refresh rate - 1 FPS makes all the Delta fluctuations and overall FPS locked to 89 with occasional 88 and 90 FPS. Then more interestingly, setting it to refresh rate - 1 then back to only refresh rate seems to make it stable at refresh rate for a little bit only to return to unstable behaviour.

Things I haven't been able to rule out is if it is headset related issue, I only have a Quest 3 to test with and it could be an issue with this Quest 3 in specific.

The biggest issue with these stutters are that they are especially noticeable in VR when having smooth movement which really affects the player.

Here is in my current project I am working on. For context this was recorded on Standalone Quest 3. Blue hands are ghost hands and are parented to XR Controller. Other hands are rigid bodies controlled through physics process. You can see noticable stuttering on the physics hands but also the cubes in the background (controlled through process). Resolution is very low to rule out performance issues.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26c13f11-4eaf-4af1-af29-4c5743f16f95

### Steps to reproduce

Have any OpenXR project and play it in VR, as far as I have been able to find.

MRP How to use:

1. On your right hand is a screen that shows relevant stats.
2. Using right controller stick you can move around the Godot Icon cursor to click things. And to click use X button (On Quest Controller) (Drop down box renders in front of cursor and I couldn't fix it)
3. There are boxes floating moving using Delta (Green) and Physics Delta (Orange), such that you can observe any stuttering however you need a very keen eye or screen record and slow down the footage.
4. There are prints that print when the delta < refresh rate - small threshold or delta > refresh rate + small threshold showing what the delta was when it happened compared to what it should be.
5. Additionally you can build for Standalone VR, works for Quest 3.
Refresh rate limiter reference: 

1. Unlimited options sets Engine.max_fps = 0
2. Refresh rate option sets Engine.max_fps = xr interface refresh rate.
3. Refresh rate -1 option sets Engine.max_fps = xr interface refresh rate - 1. So 90hz = 89hz
